summary: Milestone 2026.05.256 recorded 0 experiments within the timing-script look-back window, making this the thirty-first consecutive empty-timing-window retro. Both RTX 3090 GPUs remained idle at 0% utilization (41C / 50C), with no compute-bound tasks visible to the timing script. The persistent conductor zero-execution stall continues unchanged; the structural fix (anchoring the timing-script look-back to conductor-state.json activation timestamp) has been identified across many prior milestones but not yet applied.
bottlenecks_identified: Timing-script look-back window not anchored to conductor-state.json activation timestamp: experiments completed within the milestone window are invisible to the retro, producing false zero-experiment reports for the thirty-first consecutive milestone.

Conductor zero-execution stall: the retro task fires before the conductor has dispatched and completed any substantive experiments, leaving both RTX 3090 GPUs idle at 0% utilization throughout the milestone window.
No post-activation dispatch verification gate: there is no mechanism that halts milestone closure and retro firing if zero substantive experiments have completed since activation.
improvements_suggested: Anchor timing-script look-back window to conductor-state.json activation timestamp so all experiments completed within the milestone window are counted in the retro.
Wire a conductor zero-artifact alarm at 60 min post-activation: if no experiment result artifact has landed in results/ since activation, raise a blocking alert before the retro fires.
Introduce a milestone-open sentinel commit at activation time to provide a reliable timing anchor independent of the look-back window mechanism.
Add a post-activation dispatch verification step: after conductor activates a milestone, verify at least one non-retro, non-capstone task has been dispatched before the retro task is eligible to run.
Treat the timing-script look-back fix as a MANDATORY precondition for milestone activation (add to the activation-guard checklist) rather than a milestone task that can be deferred.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Fix timing-script look-back to use conductor-state.json activation timestamp as the start boundary — eliminates the false-zero reporting pattern that has persisted for 31 consecutive milestones at near-zero implementation cost.
Wire conductor zero-artifact alarm at 60 min post-activation to interrupt the retro firing sequence if no substantive experiment artifact has landed, forcing diagnosis before milestone close.
Require a milestone-open commit at conductor activation as a sentinel so the timing boundary is always deterministic and auditable from git history alone.
meta_reflection: Thirty-one consecutive empty-timing-window retros indicate the identified root cause (look-back window not anchored to activation timestamp) has been correctly diagnosed but is itself blocked by the conductor stall — the fix is not being applied because the conductor that would apply it is not executing tasks. Treating the timing-script repair as a MANDATORY activation precondition rather than a scheduled experiment task is the only path that breaks this cycle. GPU health (41C/50C, 0% utilization) confirms the hardware layer is fully operational and ready; the bottleneck is entirely in the software-process layer above it.
